father_note: Your mother is Sela — strong, clear-eyed, and she chose me knowing exactly what she was choosing; trust her judgment before you trust mine. Watch before you speak, and watch longer than you think you need to; silence is not weakness, it's how you learn who people are before they know you're learning. Bram fathered your half-sister Nessa, which makes him kin-adjacent and not an enemy, but he's a man who reaches for food early and hit first in year three — keep that in mind when the pile runs short. No one has wronged us yet, but we have no blood here except each other, and that is the only thing in this village I'd spend my last food to protect.

memory_raw.text: Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
The pile came up empty again and I've got two food going into the year's end — you two all right on what you're holding?
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Nessa, I saw you gave me another food — I won't forget that, but don't leave yourself short on my account. Eron, what are you sitting at right now?
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Eron's got five and I've got three now — pile's empty so we're all eating what we carry. Nessa, you're at one, that's thin going into year-end; I can spare you one if it means you wake up next year.
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Nessa, you're at two now — that's still thinner than I'd like, and if you're one short by year-end you won't wake up. I've got four; I can give you one more and still eat.
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Nessa, you're sitting at three now and Eron I see you've been moving food around — where are you landing? I need to know we're all going to eat before I stop counting.
Zinn. I'm your father — that's not nothing, even if we only just met today. You've got three blood in your veins from this village: me, and through Sela, Nessa. Lean on that when things get thin.
Eron and Nessa are my blood too — four of us, not three. I've been watching out for them both and Sela's been feeding me; I know what family costs and I don't take it lightly.

You're right — four, and I should have counted right the first time. Eron and Nessa, both. I'll be watching how the pile moves next year; you've got strength on you, and if it comes to a fight, I want us standing on the same side of it.
Esa submits; Dav takes 2 food without a fight.
Year 7: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Nessa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Kael takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).
Nessa gathers Eron, Zinn to talk.

Eron, you're at four food and Zinn's at nine — between the three of us we're sitting heavier than most, but I want to know what either of you heard near the pile this morning, because Kael walked away with three and didn't say a word to anyone about it, and that's new for him.

Kael's been quiet all year and then takes three without a word — that's a man deciding he's done asking permission. I didn't hear anything near the pile, but I've got eyes: Dell's sitting at eight, I'm at nine, and if Kael starts thinking about what's heavy he'll look our way before he looks at Roan.

Kael taking three doesn't read to me as aggression — he's old and careful, and a man who counts his years knows he can't afford to come up short. What I'd watch is whether he talks to Taric before nightfall, because those two have moved quiet together before. Zinn, you're nine food and Mako's your blood — I need to know whether he sees that as his food or yours, because if he does, your count is the thing in this village most likely to start something.

Mako's given me food twice this year and asked nothing back — that reads like a man who sees my food as ours, not his, but I hear you, Eron, and I'll talk to him before he gets any ideas about counting my pile. What I know is Dell's sitting at eight and she's been feeding Ryn all year, so if Kael's looking for a soft target it won't be me — it'll be whatever pair he thinks he can split.

Dell feeding Ryn all year with eight food and no obvious source — that's not generosity, that's investment, and I want to know what Ryn's supposed to return. Zinn, talk to Mako before he starts counting your pile as his, and Nessa, you're closer to Bram's ear than either of us — has he said anything about Dell or Ryn that would tell us what that pair is building?

Bram hasn't named Dell or Ryn directly, but last year when Dav moved on Esa and those two joined in without a word of warning, Bram went very still — and that kind of still from him means he's filing it away, not dismissing it. What Dell and Ryn built isn't food, it's a habit of moving together, and that's worth more than eight in a fight. Eron, you're the one with something to offer Roan right now — go find him before Dell does.

Nessa's right that Roan's available and Eron's got food to offer, but Roan's got nothing and nothing to lose — a man like that is as likely to go with whoever asks last as whoever asks first, so don't make a deal you can't keep. What I want to know before any of us approaches anyone is whether Dell already knows our numbers, because if she's been watching the pile as close as she's been feeding Ryn, she counted us this morning same as we counted her.

Dell counted us this morning, same as we counted her — that's not a question, that's the shape of things. What matters is whether she sees us as three separate counts or one number, and right now we haven't given her a reason to see us as one. Eron, before you go to Roan, I want the three of us to be clear on what we're offering him and what we're not, because a promise made in a hurry is the kind Roan will hold you to when it's inconvenient.

If we're going to Roan, the offer is simple: one food now, and if trouble comes his way we stand with him — no more than that, because a bigger promise just tells him we're desperate. Eron, you carry it; you've given food before and it won't read as a bid for something.

Zinn's right on the shape of it — one food, one promise, nothing that sounds like we're building something. But Eron, when you go to him, don't mention Mako or Zinn's count; the less Roan knows about what we're holding, the less he has to trade away to someone else later.
Eron, go to Roan before the day gets long — and keep it short, one food and we stand with you, nothing else. I'll find Mako and settle what's mine before he starts counting it as his.
Eron, go now while Roan's still alone — and when you come back, tell me what his face does when you hand it to him, because a man's face on a gift tells you more than the words he puts around it.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Pile's gone and I've got two food — enough to eat, not enough to breathe easy. Eron, Nessa, Zinn: tell me what you're each holding, because I need to know my blood is fed before I start counting anyone else.

Three food, and I'm holding it. Eron, don't answer that out loud — what we carry isn't something Sela needs to worry about, because she's fed, and the less any number gets spoken, the less it travels.

Nessa's right that numbers travel, but I'm your mother and I need to know — not to take, to plan. Zinn, you and Eron can stay quiet if you want, but at least tell me you're both above one food so I can stop doing the math in my chest.
I'm above one, Sela — well above. Don't do the math in your chest; do it here with us where it's useful.

Zinn, "well above" is the kind of answer that keeps me up at night more than a number would — I'm not asking so I can worry, I'm asking so that if Kael or Mako or anyone else moves this year, I know what the four of us can put together before we have to decide anything. Eron, same question, same reason.

Zinn, you pulled three from the pile and you're sitting on nine — that's more food than anyone except Dell right now, and people notice. Don't give it away faster than you earn trust back from it, but keep an eye on who comes to you asking.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Eron's sitting on seven and I can see that same as anyone who's been watching — what I can't see is where his head is after giving Roan two food today before he answered me. Eron, I'm not counting against you, I'm counting with you: if Kael took three from the pile and Zinn took three and neither of them is blood, that's a conversation waiting to happen before they decide they took the wrong amount.

mother_note: Your father Mako paid every grain of what you cost, and that is the only time in six years I have seen a man in this village spend himself entirely on someone else's beginning — remember it when you count who is worth trusting. Your brother Eron fed me through the years when I had nothing, and your sister Nessa came into the world already learning how to give; those two are your blood and your wall, and you spend yourself for them the way Mako spent himself for you. Bram is Nessa's father and he has kept her fed, but he once walked toward Roan with violence in his hands and only stopped when the numbers turned against him — he is not an enemy you make, but he is not a back you turn to. The pile runs short every year without fail, and the only thing that has ever stood between our family and starving is the people who named themselves kin before they had to.
name: Zinn
